notes.text: OFFICIAL ARTBOOK

Since Reverse: 1999 was released, several years have passed up to today. The game's setting and tone have never stopped; instead, walking alongside all of you, they have grown and calibrated together with the tight update rhythm of every version, heading toward a more distant future. This brand-new and enduring test has once again granted us (as well as this web-like, intricately woven lore) endless vitality.

Re-exploring, collecting, and repeatedly proofreading the vast and diverse world of Reverse: 1999 was a huge challenge, yet it also allowed us to look back on that period filled with the heart's blood, talent, and youthful ideals of all the creators. Here, we sincerely invite you to turn to the next page and feel with us that surging tide of curiosity and passion.

This setting book is a gift from us to you—that legendary figure who once witnessed the roaring torrent of manus and walked against the "Storm," constantly chasing the dawn amid the tragedy—a tiny "footnote" about this world. 


— T. Tou, Game Content Director of Reverse: 1999

The "Storm" setting of Reverse: 1999 was born on a sudden, pouring night filled with the untamed, tropical wilderness atmosphere of southern China. The olive branch of fate was tossed our way—the company placed almost no creative restrictions on the project, only encouraging us to unleash our inspiration as much as possible. So, we decided to tackle a theme that hadn't appeared on the market at the time, and make a game that we ourselves would be willing to boldly explore and wholeheartedly enjoy. From that moment on, this project—carrying a simple, wild ambition—was destined to face many unexpected "firsts" and gigantic challenges.

On that blank sheet of paper holding countless possibilities of imagination, the very first things we locked down were the most practical and indispensable elements: gameplay and audience. Afterward, the world-view system, major historical chronicles, and artistic aesthetic style gradually took shape and emerged one after another as the team came together. The thematic definition of "20th-century retro occultism" step by step deduced surrealism, modern aesthetic sensibilities, cinematic texture, systematic occultism, and more—keywords that had circulated only internally. Together, they wrote the team's subconscious text and became the "lore" and "tone" we talk about every day. It was precisely these shared understandings that drove us to make, without hesitation, one decision after another that seemed uniquely independent at the time. They permeate every corner of the game: whether it is the graphic design language, the dreamy or neo-classical musical style, or even the ultimate truth revealed by the world-view—all of our oars were pulling with all their might in the exact same direction.

When it arrives, time is rendered insignificant.
Time flows back to the past, time returns to the future.
Or there is nothingness,
Or rebirth through raging fire
"Storm" Syndrome

"Storm Syndrome" is an anomalous phenomenon that occurs before a "Storm" takes place. It affects people, objects, and events, often accompanied by symptoms that drive individuals insane. The external pathological characteristics of Storm Syndrome are frequently related to the art of the era or major historical events. Under the scouring of the "Storm," the order of the world becomes unrecognizable; everything begins to trend toward madness, heading toward derivation [or proliferation]. Swallowing gold alive, craving petroleum, dancing and singing on sizzling hot iron plates. The sufferers never know they are sick—it is the same at any given time.

(1) Storm Syndrome alters the physical characteristics of victims, and sometimes changes their cognition; there is no single uniform symptom.
(2) The effects of Storm Syndrome act not only on people but also impact the environment. This influence alters the composition of the environment at a physical level.
(3) Under specific circumstances, Storm Syndrome can also affect Arcanists.

(4) Storm Syndrome does not spread worldwide immediately; instead, it starts from the "Storm" critical point and expands and intensifies along with the approaching "Storm." The closer to the critical point, the more severe the symptoms. Abnormal behaviors caused by the same syndrome may vary slightly due to regional cultural differences, but the physical manifestations—aside from the degree—are basically identical.

A phenomenon of temporal and spatial disaster, characterized by rain falling from the sky and then flowing backward into the air, causing an entire “era” to undergo a “regression.”
After a “Storm,” the world enters an “era” different from the one that existed before

The occurrence of a “Storm” goes through the following stages:
1.	Strange phenomena begin to appear.
2.	Rain falls from the sky.
3.	Signs of a Storm emerge.
4.	Rainwater begins flowing backward into the sky.
5.	The “Storm” officially occurs, and the era is “reversed.”

Social conflicts, historical changes, and the emergence of new technologies can all cause a “Storm” to occur. Human intervention can accelerate its occurrence.
After a “Storm,” the entire world undergoes an “era regression.” However, the direction of this regression is not necessarily toward the past; it may also move forward. Its underlying rules remain unknown.
Asymmetric Nuclide R

A substance discovered in the raindrops of a “Storm.” It disappears very quickly after appearing and exists in an unstable state.
1.	The earliest sample of Asymmetric Nuclide R was collected by 12-year-old Vertin  during the third “Storm,” obtained directly from its raindrops.
2.	Asymmetric Nuclide R is commonly present in the atmosphere 24 hours before a “Storm” begins. During this time, enormous amounts of arcane energy are generated in the atmosphere, forming a gigantic magical array. This spiritually charged environment can overcome the bloodline restrictions normally imposed on rituals, allowing arcanists to release higher-level magic.

3.	Direct contact with unstable Asymmetric Nuclide R causes damage and deformation to hair and skin tissue.
4.	Using a sound-wave generator at a fixed frequency to stimulate Asymmetric Nuclide R can partially simulate the environment of a “Storm.”

5.	In arcanum visualization experiments, Asymmetric Nuclide R exhibits a bifurcated structure.
6.	Stable Asymmetric Nuclide R exists in the Reshaping Mask. Its immunity to “Storms” may be related to this substance.
7.	The Research Center has attempted to inject Asymmetric Nuclide R into the Balancing Mask to prevent its wearer from becoming infected with Storm Syndrome. However, this function has not yet been verified.

A general term for the abilities and techniques that only the arcanist population can use, standing in contrast to the science created by the human race.
The most common application of arcanum is the use of arcane skills.

notes.title: Dust
notes.text: Tiny dust is nowhere to be found, yet its power is vast and incalculable. Within the powder shaken off by great beings lies the energy that triggers ascension/insight. In a certain sense, this dust is one corner of the ultimate answer
Arcanum / Occultism

notes.title: Sharpodonty
notes.text: A currency passed down from the ancient blank era to the present day, framed by twelve edges; its sharp, pointed teeth open only to those with arcane blood flowing through them

notes.title: Resonance
notes.text: Resonance is the act by which an arcanist spiritually understands and perceives existing, established things. Unlike "Inheritance," which comes from bloodline and heritage, Resonance is born purely from personal thought. An arcanist's way of thinking is primarily emotional/perceptual—that is, intuitive sensibility; a human's way of thinking is primarily rational analysis—that is, logical rationality. As for "mixed-blood arcanists" who blend human and arcanist bloodlines, those whose bloodline is still fairly normal also use "Resonance," whereas those with lower arcanist bloodline purity, as well as pure-blooded humans, use "Inspiration."

An innate talent—like the radiance in a wine cellar that will never fade.
Wondrous gifts lie hidden within the minds of arcanists, just like bloodlines or what ought to flow through their veins, often accompanied by mysterious patterns; their power varies from person to person, and their uses can be large or small—sometimes bringing convenience, and sometimes bringing long, wry smiles and irreversible trouble.

notes.title: Psychube
notes.text:
Psychube is one of the essential physiological traits of an arcanist. Even a mixed-blood individual with the smallest trace of arcanist bloodline possesses this trait.
Psychube includes two outward/manifest constants: Imaging and Amplitude.
Imaging: The impression generated by the mind—that is, an externalized image formed by different emotions, experiences, viewpoints, and thoughts. Roentgen-ray psychube detectors and crystal divination are common methods for imaging.
Amplitude: The amplitude of the psychube—that is, the wave intensity and flicker produced by psychube fluctuations. Psychube amplitude measurement is a mandatory subject in the Foundation's annual graduation exam, and Sonnetto set the highest record in this subject.

A race capable of using arcane skills; they can cast arcane skills by consuming cellular activity. This race has gradually declined, becoming progressively marginalized and forgotten after the human race grew strong.
Under the arcanist race, there are multiple subordinate branches, which are often determined by the purity and origin of their bloodline.
"A race remembered by the world for its talent, so as to be distinguished from other ordinary people. No one knows why arcanists became arcanists; they once flourished, and now have declined."

Among the descendants of humans and arcanists, individuals with a relatively diluted arcanist bloodline are called Mixed-Blood Arcanists.
There appears to be an atavistic (skip-a-generation) inheritance phenomenon, whereby an arcanist can be born into a human family that carries arcanist bloodline
Pure-blood arcanists are far stronger in their ability to use arcane skills than non-purebloods; bloodline purity and arcane skill capability have a linear relationship

Arcanists who become infected after coming into contact with Critters and transform into Infected Arcanists.

Once the transformation is complete, the subject gains the arcane abilities of the corresponding infected strain, though most die due to physical and mental collapse.

Most Awakened do not have flesh or nerves; they are merely a segment of "primordial consciousness" or motion attached to an object. Because the vessels of the Awakened are mostly non-biological matter, their lineage is often related to their composition and energy source.
Not all Awakened possess the same organs as humans; for example, Ms. Radio does not vocalize on her own, which is because she lacks vocal organs.
To facilitate movement, some Awakened attach external extension units to the core containing their primordial consciousness.
Whether the Awakened possess biological sex remains unclear, but on a cognitive level, most Awakened perceive gender as existing.
Some arcanists are born from the manifestation of cultural concepts; although these arcanists have undergone an awakening process, they do not belong to the Awakened.

Demons, blood-clan monsters, and vampiric mermaids are all categorized under the "Beyond" classification.
There exist arcanists from beyond Earth; such arcanists are often classified as Beyond.

Human ancestors are said to have been born at the exact moment the Blank Era ended; humans gradually replaced arcanists to become the dominant race.

Perception of Arcanum:
Lacking arcanist talent, humans are generally unable to interact with concepts within arcanum, though there are those among humans who understand and research arcanum.
Humans are not adept at intuitive insight, excelling instead at logical deduction based on observation.
There is a certain overlap between arcanum and human science, which allowed some arcane techniques to become the ancient predecessors of science.

A lively arcanist sports gathering originating from the Blank Era. The Games are held once a year, with the specific dates determined according to the Sacred Flame and the Uluru Games [Committee/tradition]. Comprising various specialized arcane competitive events and arcane exhibition events, it was once widely popular in the arcane world. Later, affected by the flames of war and racial antagonism, the Games vanished into history, and its ruins disappeared without a trace.
Through the cooperation of the Reincarnator Spathodea, Laplace researcher Ezra, and others, everyone found the ruins of the Games and the Sacred Flame, reviving the spirit of the Games. From this point on, the torch of the Games will be passed down year after year.

The Dushuo Festival begins on the 24th day of the twelfth lunar month  and lasts until the 15th day of the first lunar month. Among these, the 30th day of the twelfth month and the first day of the following month are New Year's Eve and the New Moon Day, when the festive atmosphere is at its richest. Every year from New Year's Eve to the first day of the first lunar month is the time when the duty gods rotate their yearly shifts and usher in the new year, which is also the origin of the people's celebrations.
Legend has it that as the passing years turn, arcanists of different Afflatuses receive a calling from the duty god of the year and are revealed their fate for the coming year. Arcanists used to hold grand celebrations at this time to bid farewell to the past and welcome new life. The celebrations, fairs, sacrifices, and prayers were magnificent in scale, and gradually, humans joined in as well.

As a general term for a class of weird creatures, "Critters" generally possess the following characteristics:
Most common Critters are small in size and exhibit behavioral traits of object mimicry, symbiosis, and adherence to customs.
Critters generally love glowing and shiny objects.
They generally show low intelligence and low aggressiveness; the Laplace Scientific Computing Center once conducted domestication experiments on Critters, proving that most Critter species have almost no possibility of intelligence improvement, though extremely rare exceptions may still exist.
Under specific conditions such as certain Critter populations or arcane influences, there is a possibility of mutation.

Common types of Critters have some overlap with the areas of humans and arcanists activities; they are weird and annoying little neighbors—pesky little creatures that occasionally cause trouble in daily life, though their attack power is usually low.

Meanwhile, large Critters that exist only in legends generally have fixed habitats and do not appear casually within human society.
Before the "Storm," anomalies reach the peak of their activity, which directly affects the behavior of Critters and increases their aggressiveness, causing them to expand their range of activity, flood into human living spaces, ruin crops, steal property, and occupy the corners where humans or arcanists are active.

notes.title: Relationship with Arcanists
notes.text: Aside from the utilization of a small number of Critters, the relationship between most Critters and arcanists is merely one of simple coexistence. The status of Critters among arcanists is more akin to insects or mice in the eyes of humans—mostly commensal creatures accompanying human activity (much like ants that frequently appear in houses). Of course, they can have other uses, and they are neither rare nor precious, appearing with no great frequency in human or arcanist settlements. Some Critters also hold value as food or for fulfilling certain functions, and most arcanists are able to accept eating Critters.

Newspapers frequently publish incidents involving damage to human society, and some tabloid media are keen on spreading and reporting news about all sorts of bizarre products of out-of-control arcanists, heretical cults, and the like; after the "Storm" appeared, Critters and other arcane creatures frequently showed up in sighting incidents. In modern times, news such as "Critter Sneaks into Refrigerator at Midnight" has become countless, occupying the small corners of newspaper pages.

Aside from the utilization of a small number of Critters, the relationship between most Critters and arcanists is merely one of simple coexistence. The status of Critters among arcanists is more akin to insects or mice in the eyes of humans—mostly commensal creatures accompanying human activity (much like ants that frequently appear in houses). Of course, they can have other uses, and they are neither rare nor precious, appearing with no great frequency in human or arcanist settlements. Some Critters also hold value as food or for fulfilling certain functions, and most arcanists are able to accept eating Critters.

notes.title: The Pax House
notes.text: The Pax Security Council (Human Peace and Security Council)

You have certainly heard of that snow-white stone house suspended high above. The textbooks tell us that it is the Pax Security Council, the current supreme governing body of Earth. They do not directly manage human society, appearing only at critical moments concerning survival and development.

The Pax House seems to possess the ability to use pigeons for surveillance and transmitting messages. These white pigeons composed of plaster are called "the pigeons of the white stone house" by high-ranking officials in the know.
An organization under the Pax Security Council, an international body responsible for the discovery, containment, management, and utilization of arcanists, arcane items, and the like.

"Within a quarter of an hour after the silver bell rings, loyal companions stand lined up here in waiting. A peacekeeping organization active around the world, and the container and manager of arcanists, arcane items, and arcane phenomena. You can safely entrust your child to the St. Pavlov Foundation; he will become a good child here."

The St. Pavlov Foundation is an international organization with the Joint Committee at its core, establishing the Communion Faction and other departments as well as subordinate agencies beneath it, with branches and affiliated offices built in various regions. Subordinate agencies include field organizations such as the Outsourced Contract Talent Management Organization, the School of Primary Defense serving as an educational institution, the Night Watch Special Operations Management Bureau responsible for preventing and investigating arcanist criminal cases, and the Timekeeper Squad which holds an independent establishment.

1. The Foundation is dedicated to safeguarding the human world and promoting social relations between arcanists and human groups, though internal attitudes and views on this differ.
2. The organization is committed to discovering, containing, and utilizing the world's remaining arcane power; the occurrence of the "Storm" has made this duty even more vital.
3. "May peace be with us, may peace be with mankind" is the Foundation's fundamental creed; the Peace Declaration based on this creed states that "regardless of physical health, wealth or poverty, or racial differences, one should extend a helping hand to maintain Earth's peaceful order."
4. The Foundation's guiding policy is to implement the "Peace Policy" and promote the integration of arcane technology into human society. Every year, the Foundation incurs massive expenditures for arcanum-related culture and education.
5. The Foundation restricts arcanists through discipline and control; some members believe that malignant incidents in history stemmed from the restless nature of arcanists, and therefore controls cannot be relaxed.
6. Numerous ideologies and factions exist within the Foundation; the contradictions in their demands and beliefs are fracturing the Foundation's convictions, and after the "Storm" occurred, factions such as human supremacism began to rise.
In accordance with the "Containment Management Regulations," the St. Pavlov Foundation registers and manages arcanists of various risk levels, and strives to promote integration between races.

One of the subordinate agencies of the St. Pavlov Foundation, providing education for underage arcanists and using specific educational methods to enhance students' understanding of arcanum, helping them form sound and reliable values. More than half of its graduating students go on to serve in the Foundation, mostly as frontline investigators.

1. In certain respects, the Foundation intentionally restricts staff members' awareness of the "Storm.
2. The Foundation conceals the existence of the "Storm" from the masses of each era through methods including, but not limited to, controlling the media, and only screens specific candidates of value.
3. The "Storm" is a strictly forbidden term within the School of Primary Defense under its jurisdiction; students who mention it receive detention, while staff members are escorted away.

1. The "Storm" emergency system was established after the second "Storm." Proposed by Lucy, the head of Laplace at the time, and jointly built with the Foundation, the system includes the following steps:
-Establish contact with all branches in the current era and tally deployable manpower.
-Establish observation stations worldwide to search for other areas immune to the "Storm."
-Establish multiple workshops to deduce the causes of the "Storm."

2. After the third "Storm," the Foundation established the Timekeeper to provide authoritative reports and records of outside time.
3. Because social conflicts, historical turmoil, the birth of new technologies, and other factors can trigger or accelerate the "Storm," the Foundation assigned outsourced contract teams the duty of forecasting the "Storm's" tipping point—a duty distinct from that of dispatched investigators.
4. During the ninth "Storm," the Scientific Computing Center developed "Storm"-immune protective gear—the Equilibrium Umbrella. Some senior investigators are issued samples, while others can obtain an Equilibrium Umbrella through application.

1. The Foundation has established corresponding processing standards and containment procedures for "Storm" survivors.
2. After a "Storm," the Foundation arranges new era-appropriate identities for headquarters staff and dispatches investigators to collect arcane materials, equipment, preservable arcane skills, and high-level technical talent from that era based on retained records.
3. Before a "Storm" occurs, field personnel are ordered to abandon their missions and return to headquarters for shelter. Before taking shelter, they must undergo an inspection procedure to screen for the effects of "Storm" syndrome; those severely affected by "Storm" syndrome are quarantined and have their movements restricted.
4. Given the limited space at headquarters, unregistered non-essential personnel, including family members, are prohibited from entering headquarters.
5. During the "Storm" countdown, the Foundation conducts an internal inventory of its preserved era collections and historical records.

An identification badge obtained by Foundation members upon formal onboarding. With this ID card, one can enter and exit areas permitted by their rank. If the ID card is lost, a loss report must be submitted before going through the replacement process.
A passport-like pass carried by Foundation field personnel. The basic information on this credential differs from an ID card, displaying only job title, name, and signature.

A specialized communicator issued to Foundation field personnel with diverse functions, capable of communication, enemy detection, and identifying abnormal fluctuations in surrounding arcane skills. Different functions are unlocked based on the user's clearance level.

Chess is Constantine's most beloved sport; she excels at it just as she is well-versed in the art of power and politics
On the final day of 1999, the "Storm" washed away nearly everything, replaced by foolish despair and ignorance. A chessboard named Fate unfolded amidst the recklessly backward-flowing time, and within it lay the very moment requiring someone to hold the pieces.
As the final piece fell, she saw that the people had become pure white chess pieces, their faces filled with youthfulness, crimson blood... they served as part of something grand, as the price to be paid.

During our creative process, Constantine was conceived as Vertin's antithesis. She is a thorough political creature; years of political experience have made her adept at weighing the value behind every emotion. To her, only by fathoming others' emotions without exposing oneself can one effortlessly control the situation.

Constantine has always believed the Foundation is overly tolerant toward arcanists—they are uncontrollable, manic, and disorderly. Yet the Foundation not only accommodates these flaws, it dotes upon these people. While the outside world may harbor prejudices against arcanists, years of political experience make Constantine far more inclined to view this as an opportunity.

Constantine's symbolic motif is the white lily.
Codename Z

Her real name is Zhang Zhizhi, but the character "之" in her name was mistakenly read as "Z" by the British. Following the trend of studying abroad, the outstanding student Z chose to study at Imperial College London, hoping to return home and contribute to her family's development. Due to her exceptional scientific achievements and research into the arcane, Z successfully received an invitation from the foundation. From then on, this bright figure moved tirelessly between gray and white buildings, striving for her ideals and her eventual return to her homeland

"Ambitious young lady who went abroad to study in response to the trend of studying abroad, and who came from engineering disciplines"—this was our initial idea when we created Ms. Zhang Zhizhi. You can find a certain lingering charm of "gentleness, kindness, respect, frugality, and humility" in her, but for us, equally important is the sharpness hidden beneath that gentleness. Carrying a thermos all year round, keeping jasmine tea bags on her desk, and not drinking unboiled water—these kinds of quirks always arouse the curiosity and learning of her colleagues.

She was free from self-interest or partisan political prejudice, which earned her widespread popularity among different factions within the St. Pavlov Foundation. She argued vehemently for her ideals and initiatives, yet disregarded the slander and defamation of certain interest groups.
In her brief few years at the Foundation, she has set foot in the School of Primary Defense, the Laplace Scientific Computing Center, the Zeno Armaments Academy, and more; she conversed happily with the still-young intern registrar, Laplace researchers, and Foundation committee members. She grew up fast—so fast that even her former ideals could not keep pace with her footsteps. Although we may have regrettably lost a great physicist, perhaps we are able to welcome a true politician.

Full name Greta Hofmann, a dispatched investigator from Germany and an anthropologist. She holds a firm conviction in the Foundation's ideal of "advancing the progress of all humanity." Hofmann is the older sister of Laplace researcher Enigma; she frequently writes letters to Enigma, sharing the world after the "Storm."

Hofmann is a protagonist of the main story special chapter "The Star"; we sought to interpret and witness this disaster through the perspective of an ordinary human investigator of the Foundation. Thus, Hofmann carries both the radiance of human rationality and the despair when rationality faces the collapse of order, as well as the selflessness and courage to still choose to shoulder responsibility after despair.
Hofmann and Enigma, this sister and brother, serve as foils to one another; both are loyal to their inner rationality and principles. Although they share the same beliefs and are both willing to strive for them, they truly lacked communication, to the point of causing misunderstandings between family members. (Yet both firmly believe in the strength of their bond!)
The story of "E lucevan le stelle" was actually created before "The Star"; in Version 1.7 she appeared as a "been-there-done-that" mentor, whereas the special chapter revealed a softer, more emotional, and more lost side of her youth. ("The Star" pays homage to Arthur C. Clarke's short story of the same name.)
Hofmann is German, yet she also possesses a certain quirky sense of humor, even though it is unintentional. Hofmann can always see through Marcus's problems at a glance and point out their essence. At the same time, however, she indulges her student; hoping that Marcus can grow in an arcanist's way that better suits her own nature, she offers only rational, limited advice.

A scientific research institution under the Pax Security Council; through a research and development direction that combines human technology and arcanum, it is dedicated to research that enables humans to use arcane technology.

"All things have cause and effect, and the world returns to unity. Aiming to deeply research future technology as well as the integration of technology and arcane skills, providing possibilities for the development of arcanum and humanity. The Scientific Computing Center rose to prominence during the course of several industrial revolutions, and its current primary goal is to propel the arrival of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR)."

Laplace employees' identification documents include formal employee badges and temporary badges for interns. These badges grant the holder specific authority and allow access to areas permitted by their job duties.

Compared to early hypnotherapy, Artificial Somnambulism technology allows the user to enter a deep hypnotic state. Through auditory stimulation and guidance, it directionally induces reactions such as imagination, memories, and emotions.

-During Artificial Somnambulism, certain specific fragments from past memories can activate trauma fragments, leading to treatment failure.
-In addition to hypnotherapy, Artificial Somnambulism technology can also be used for combat simulation, training, and assessment. These functions require the user to perform specific physical movements to activate on the machine. The simulated combat function allows multiple people to train simultaneously and can increase training difficulty.

notes.title: Currently known simulation programs for Artificial Somnambulism include:

notes.text:
-Once Artificial Somnambulism begins, the user feels "an invisible fluid being blocked," after which simulated scenes appear in their field of vision.
-Artificial Somnambulism technology is also used to manufacture weapons; some of the Foundation's guard captains are equipped with weapons produced via Artificial Somnambulism.

An item used by Foundation personnel to store and cast arcane skills. Materialized incantations that have been thoroughly mastered can be stored inside it. Different incantations require floppy disks made of different materials for storage.

-Developed by the Scientific Computing Center to collect samples of Asymmetric Nuclide R, designed specifically for its property of rapidly vanishing without a trace.
-If the test-paper tube inside the device turns gold after absorbing a sample, it indicates that Asymmetric Nuclide R has been collected. The speed of color change corresponds to the concentration of Asymmetric Nuclide R in the sample.

notes.title: "Storm"-immune protective gear developed by the Scientific Computing Center; its structure consists of the following three parts:
notes.text:
-—Ritual Core: A materialized ritual of the "Storm"-immunity incantation (i.e., the Hoffman Knot). It prevents the user from being reversed, though it is limited by cases where the user's spiritual capacity is insufficient to meet casting requirements, as well as curse side effects.
-—Converter: Improved from X's Equilibrium Headpiece technology, it can generate an equilibrium field from the atmosphere filled with arcane energy prior to the "Storm," allowing the user to meet the casting conditions.
-—Harmonizer: Its totem originates from the Equilibrium Scroll, utilizing its property of "bridging the spiritual chasm" to neutralize curse effects.
As it is still in the testing phase, the first-generation Equilibrium Umbrella can only effectively prevent 162 types of side effects.
